title: A finite union of affine closed subschemes is affine
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r\hookrightarrow Y$ be affine closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose underlying sets cover $Y$ (the empty family is allowed when $Y=\varnothing$). Then $Y$ is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: Case $r=0$. Then the $Z_i$ cover nothing, so the underlying set of $Y$ is empty and $Y$ is the empty scheme. The empty scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the zero ring (the zero ring has no prime ideals), so $Y\cong\operatorname{Spec}(0)$ is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. From now on $r\ge1$.

Let $i_j:Z_j\to Y$ ($1\le j\le r$) be the closed immersions and let $W=Z_1\amalg\cdots\amalg Z_r$ be the disjoint union (coproduct) of schemes, with the induced morphism $\pi=(i_1,\ldots,i_r):W\to Y$ (the source's $\coprod Z_i\to X$). Since each $Z_j$ is affine, $W$ is a finite disjoint union of affine schemes and hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (4).

$\pi$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Each closed immersion $i_j$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. Induction on $k=1,\ldots,r$: put $W_k=Z_1\amalg\cdots\amalg Z_k$ and $\pi_k=(i_1,\ldots,i_k):W_k\to Y$. For $k=1$, $\pi_1=i_1$ is finite. For $k\ge2$, $W_k=W_{k-1}\amalg Z_k$ (associativity of the coproduct) and $\pi_k=(\pi_{k-1},i_k)$ is the morphism induced by the two finite morphisms $\pi_{k-1}$ (induction hypothesis) and $i_k$, so it is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct]. Hence $\pi=\pi_r$ is finite. (The source says $\pi$ is integral; finite is stronger, and is what the next step uses.)

$\pi$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]: the underlying set of $W$ is the disjoint union of those of the $Z_j$ and $\pi$ restricts to $i_j$ on $Z_j$, so the image of $\pi$ is $\bigcup_j i_j(Z_j)$, which is all of $Y$ by hypothesis. $\pi$ is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism], since a finite morphism is universally closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] (1).
So $\pi:W\to Y$ is a surjective, universally closed morphism with affine source $W$ (steps 2-4). By Proposition 05YU [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-affine-target], $Y$ is affine.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks Limits Lemma 09NL (limits.tex, label lemma-affines-glued-in-closed-affine; tag verified in tags/tags) and its proof: the disjoint union of the Z_i maps surjectively and integrally onto X with affine source, so X is affine by Proposition 05YU (limits-proposition-affine, tag verified). The source's proof does not use an ideal-product reduction to two closed subschemes or Serre's criterion; the split follows the source. Steps: r=0 (empty scheme = Spec 0); the coproduct W is affine (finite disjoint union of affines); pi: W -> Y is finite (closed immersions finite, 035C; induction with the binary coproduct of finite morphisms, 0CYI), which is stronger than the source's 'integral'; pi is surjective (elementary) and universally closed (finite => universally closed, 01WN); conclude by the existing 05YU node. Statement kept. No new node: every fact is an existing node (four Mathlib leaves and the 05YU node).
